freeAgeCalculatorEnter: Free age calculator: enter a date of birth to get the exact age in years, months and days, plus the time left until the next birthday.
freeFdCalculatorEnter: Free FD calculator: enter your deposit, interest rate, tenure and compounding to see the fixed deposit maturity amount and interest earned.
thisIsAnEstimateBefore: This is an estimate before tax. Banks may count days, treat a part-period differently or round at other steps, so your bank's figure can differ slightly.
howFixedDepositInterest: How fixed deposit interest is calculated
yesTheSameStatedRate: Yes. The same stated rate earns more when interest is added more often. The effective annual yield shown under the result is the rate you actually earn per year after compounding.
yesInterestIsAdded: Yes. Interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate, and the bank may deduct TDS once interest crosses a threshold. This calculator shows interest before any tax.
whatIfMyFdPays: What if my FD pays interest out regularly instead of at maturity?
aPayoutNonCumulativeFd: A payout (non-cumulative) FD does not compound, because the interest leaves the deposit. Its total interest is closer to simple interest, so choose the compounding that matches your FD type.
whyDoesMyBankShow: Why does my bank show a slightly different amount?
banksMayUseExactDay: Banks may use exact day counts, treat the last part-period differently or round at different stages. Use this as a close estimate and confirm the final figure with your bank.
freeHomeLoanEmiCalculator: Free home loan EMI calculator: enter the loan amount, interest rate and tenure to see your monthly EMI, total interest and total payment.
freeIncomeTaxCalculator: Free income tax calculator for FY 2026-27: compare India's old and new regimes and estimate your tax, 4% cess and in-hand income.
estimateOnlyUsingTheIndividual: Estimate only, using the individual slab rates for FY 2026-27 (unchanged from FY 2025-26). The ₹75,000 / ₹50,000 standard deduction applies to salaried individuals and pensioners. Surcharge, senior-citizen slabs and other income are not included. Tax law changes every Budget — verify with the Income Tax Department or a tax professional before making real decisions.
marginalReliefAppliesYourTax: Marginal relief applies — your tax is limited to the income earned above ₹12,00,000.
rebateUnderSection87aApplies: Rebate under Section 87A applies — your tax liability is effectively nil.
seeHowInflationChangesWhat: See how inflation changes what money is worth — either what something will cost in the future, or what a future amount is worth today.
freeLumpsumCalculatorEnter: Free lumpsum calculator: enter a one-time investment, expected annual return and period to see the estimated maturity value and total gains.
thisIsAnEstimateAssuming: This is an estimate assuming a constant annual return, compounded yearly, before tax and fund charges. Actual returns fluctuate and aren't guaranteed.
itIsInvestingTheWhole: It is investing the whole amount at once, instead of a SIP where you invest a fixed amount every month. It suits money you already have available, such as a bonus, maturity proceeds or savings.
lumpsumOrSipWhich: Lumpsum or SIP — which is better?
neitherWinsForEveryone: Neither wins for everyone. A lumpsum puts all your money to work from day one, which helps if markets rise afterwards. A SIP spreads your purchases over time, which reduces the risk of investing everything just before a fall and suits a regular income. Try this calculator and the SIP calculator side by side.
noReturnIsGuaranteedPick: No return is guaranteed. Pick a conservative figure and also try lower ones to see how sensitive the result is — small changes in the rate make a large difference over long periods.
doesTheResultIncludeTax: Does the result include tax or charges?
noTheFigureIsBefore: No. The figure is before tax, expense ratio and exit loads. Your actual take-home depends on the instrument you choose and how long you hold it.
freeRdCalculatorEnter: Free RD calculator: enter a monthly deposit, interest rate and tenure to see the recurring deposit maturity amount and total interest earned.
thisIsAnEstimateBefore2: This is an estimate before tax, with interest compounded quarterly as most Indian banks do. Banks may treat a part-quarter slightly differently, so confirm the final figure with your bank.
howRecurringDepositInterest: How recurring deposit interest is calculated
anRdLetsYouDeposit: An RD lets you deposit a fixed amount every month for a chosen tenure at a fixed interest rate, and collect the total, with interest, at maturity. It builds a savings habit without needing a large starting amount.
whatHappensIfIMiss: What happens if I miss an instalment?
banksUsuallyChargeASmall: Banks usually charge a small penalty for each missed or late instalment, and some close the RD after repeated misses. The rules differ by bank, so check yours.
anRdEarnsAFixed: An RD earns a fixed, bank-declared rate, so the outcome is predictable but usually modest. A mutual fund SIP has no guaranteed return, with higher potential and higher risk. Compare both using this calculator and the SIP calculator.
yesTheInterestIsAdded: Yes. The interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate, and TDS may apply above a threshold. This calculator shows interest before tax.
estimateTheFutureValue: Estimate the future value of a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) based on your monthly contribution, expected return, and tenure.
thisIsAnEstimateAssuming2: This is an estimate assuming a constant annual return, compounded monthly. Actual mutual fund returns fluctuate and aren't guaranteed.
estimateHowMuchLifeCover: Estimate how much life cover you need to protect your family's future — based on income, liabilities, and savings.
basedOnAnnualIncomeAge: Based on {{multiplier}}× annual income (age-adjusted), plus outstanding loans, minus existing savings
thisIsACoverageNeed: This is a coverage-need estimate using the Human Life Value method, not a premium quote — actual premiums depend on the insurer, your health, and underwriting. Talk to your Insurance agent for a real quote tailored to you.
exactAgeInYearsMonths: Exact age in years, months, and days from a date of birth.
projectTheFutureValue: Project the future value of your monthly mutual fund investments.
seeWhatAOneTime: See what a one-time investment could grow to over the years.
maturityValueAndInterest: Maturity value and interest on a monthly recurring deposit.
maturityValueAndInterest2: Maturity value and interest on a fixed deposit, with your choice of compounding.
estimateYourTaxUnder: Estimate your tax under the old and new regimes.
monthlyEmiTotalInterest: Monthly EMI, total interest, and total payment on a home loan.
estimateHowMuchLifeCover2: Estimate how much life cover you actually need.
seeHowInflationAffects: See how inflation affects the value of money over time.
freeCalculatorsForAgeSip: Free calculators for age, SIP, lumpsum, FD and RD returns, income tax, home loan EMI, term insurance cover and inflation — quick tools for agents and clients alike.
quickFreeCalculatorsToPlan: Quick, free calculators to plan your finances — no account needed.
withACumulativeFd: With a cumulative FD the bank adds your interest to the deposit at regular intervals, and later interest is earned on that larger balance. Most Indian banks compound quarterly; the more often interest is added, the higher the maturity amount.
aLumpsumIsASingle: A lumpsum is a single, one-time investment. Every year the return is added to the amount, so the next year's return is earned on a bigger base — that is compounding.
pTheAmountYouInvest: P = the amount you invest today
inAnRdYouDeposit: In an RD you deposit a fixed amount every month. Each instalment earns interest only for the months it stays in the account, so earlier deposits earn more than later ones. Interest is compounded quarterly, and the maturity value is every instalment plus its interest.
